notes: Both agree on loss of spatial specificity in Tau neurons. Peer review affirms 'the contrast between poor spatial coding and strong and rigid sequence coding is compelling.' Shared claims C3, C20-C22, C24-C26.

LLM finds sequence robustness well-supported with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers raise methodological concerns about whether the method 'artificially enhances detection of rigid sequences' and extended firing periods 'could give more opportunities for short sequences.' Shared claims C4, C28-C33.

LLM finds spatial dissociation clearly demonstrated with quantitative evidence. Peer reviewers accept basic finding but request additional analysis on spatial periodicity and consistency across environments. Shared claims C34-C36.

Both agree on environment-invariance of Tau sequences. Peer reviewers affirm 'the sequence structure is retained, but the ability to bind the sequences to behavior and location is diminished.' Shared claims C41-C46.

LLM finds theta analysis sufficient to rule out theta dysfunction as primary cause. Peer reviewers request additional quantification and analysis of EEG during rigid sequences, indicating insufficient evidence. Perfect claim overlap C76-C81.

LLM concludes behavioral differences cannot explain neural sequences. Peer reviewers concerned that 'Tau animals could be more confused and turn around more' and request trajectory analysis to rule out behavioral confounds. Shared claims C69-C74.

Both uncertain about gender difference interpretation. LLM notes unclear biological interpretation and speculative explanations. Peer reviewers note discrepancy with prior literature (Yao et al 2011) requiring discussion. Shared claims C82-C84, C111.

LLM rates mechanistic interpretation (CA3 dominance over entorhinal input) as speculative requiring direct validation. Peer reviewers accept this as the study's key contribution, affirming the internal-versus-external framework. Shared claims C6-C7, C86-C94.

LLM finds model validation well-supported. Peer reviewers request clarification on cell-type specificity of neuronal loss (inhibitory vs pyramidal) and interneuron activity. Only partial overlap on claims C18-C19; peer review focuses on cell-type details not extensively covered by LLM.

Both uncertain about mechanistic details. LLM notes interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers request clarification on whether entorhinal cortex and medial septum are affected and whether CA3 is spared. Shared claims C98, C100-C102, C109.

Both agree on novel environment findings strengthening main conclusions. Peer reviewers accept that 'firing sequences are independent of external stimuli.' Shared claims include C48-C52, C54-C56, C58-C59 with partial overlap across multiple LLM results.

Both support spatial findings but with different claim groupings. LLM R5 focuses on residual spatial modulation (C60-C64), while peer R1 focuses on loss of spatial specificity. Minimal direct overlap (C48-C49) but complementary findings.

Both support environment-invariance findings. LLM R4 emphasizes track-derived sequences in open box (C41-C46, C52, C56-C59). Peer R5 accepts sequences independent of external stimuli. Partial overlap on C52, C56, C58-C59.

Both support spatial and sequence findings but different emphases. LLM R1 on spatial specificity loss (includes C48-C49). Peer R5 on sequence independence from external stimuli. Minimal overlap but complementary conclusions.

LLM finds sequence robustness supported (C50, C54 among others). Peer R5 accepts sequence structure retained. Minimal direct overlap (C50, C54) but peer review doesn't raise methodological concerns for these specific claims as in peer R2.
LLM supports spatial dissociation (C51, C55 among others). Peer R5 accepts sequences not spatially anchored. Minimal overlap (C51, C55) but complementary findings on sequence-space relationship.

LLM R5 addresses residual spatial modulation (C60-C64). Peer R6 questions whether sequence retrieval and formation are mutually exclusive (C13-C14). No direct claim overlap; different aspects of spatial-sequence relationship.
LLM R4 includes temporal ordering claims. Peer R9 questions temporal regularity of rigid sequences (C65-C67). No direct claim overlap but related to temporal aspects of sequence expression.
